steps.description: Take the DESeqDataSet built from tximport in T1S1. Set the condition factor's reference level explicitly to the control level as named in metadata.csv, so the contrast is c('condition', <lesional level>, <control level>) and a positive log2 fold change means higher expression in lesional skin — state both level names in the output. Apply the minimal pre-filter: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size). Run DESeq() with the default median-of-ratios size factors combined with the tximport length offsets — do not supply externally normalized counts. Extract results with the Wald test, alpha = 0.05, independent filtering on. Keep DESeq2's default count-outlier policy (Cook's-distance flagging with p-value set to NA, which applies at 6 replicates per cell) and report how many genes have NA p-values from outlier flagging separately from how many have NA adjusted p-values from the independent filter. Shrink the lesional-vs-control coefficient with lfcShrink type='apeglm' and keep both the unshrunken log2FoldChange with its lfcSE and the shrunken estimate in the results table. Plot the histogram of unadjusted p-values before interpreting adjusted values and describe its shape. Write out the full results table for all tested genes (gene ID, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, pvalue, padj) and the significant subset at padj < 0.05. Also report, as a secondary and clearly labelled analysis, the number of genes passing an effect-size threshold tested inside the model with lfcThreshold = 1 (results(..., lfcThreshold=1)) rather than by post-hoc filtering on the estimate. plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE from Salmon quants
plan.analytical_narrative: The inputs are per-sample Salmon quantification directories (quant.sf, 30147 transcript rows x 5 columns each) plus tx2gene.csv (30147 transcripts -> gene), and metadata.csv (12 samples x 2 columns: sample, condition), for 6 atopic dermatitis lesional skin samples vs 6 controls, unpaired, single batch, Homo sapiens. Because no gene-level count matrix was delivered and NumReads are non-integer estimates, the first thing the analysis must do is import the quantifications at gene level with tximport, keeping countsFromAbundance = no so that the average transcript length per gene and sample is carried into the negative binomial model as an offset (DESeq2's DESeqDataSetFromTximport does this); rounding TPM to counts without the length correction would introduce false calls driven by isoform usage. T1S1 builds the gene-level object and runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) so that an outlier or a control/lesional mixing is visible before any test. T1S2 fits the two-group model with an explicit reference level (control as denominator, contrast condition: lesional vs control, so positive log2 fold change = higher in lesional skin), the minimal 10-counts-in-6-samples pre-filter, DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, the Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the lesional-vs-control coefficient, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. Because n = 6 per group sits at the low end where DESeq2 and edgeR disagree on a minority of genes, T1S3 refits the same counts and offsets with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test and reports the intersection as the high-confidence set. T1S4 assembles the report: annotated gene table, MA and dispersion plots, p-value histogram, counts of NA p-values split by outlier flag versus independent filter, and the reproducibility record. No enrichment step is planned: the research question asks only which genes are differentially expressed, and gene-set analysis would be unasked scope.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
tximport gene-level import with average transcript length offset
DE report with MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, session info

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step as a whole; the reporting settings of R-0085, R-0087, R-0041, R-0042 and R-0086 are carried as the step's requirements.

flags.message: If the strandedness of the library is unknown, infer it before the counting step, and before you trust a count table that a counter made with a strand setting. Run an inference on a sample of aligned reads against the annotation, for example the infer_experiment module of RSeQC, and record the result for every sample. A wrong strand setting counts the antisense reads of an overlapping gene, or it drops half of the reads, and the sample structure QC does not show the error.
